title: impl_defaults parallelization knob names
description: The CANONICAL key names of the parallelization family inside spec.ir.yaml's impl_defaults knob layer (`abstract` and `backend_overrides`), applied by the Compile.static deterministic gate at --stage compile. This exists because the knob layer was un-pinned: four recompiles of one spec produced four different spellings of the same knob (`parallelization` as both a flat string and a mapping; the scope knob as `parallel_loop_scope` / `parallel_scope` / `parallelization_scope` / `loop_parallelization` / `parallel_loops`; the thread count as `num_threads` / `threads` / `threads_per_rank`), and only `backend_overrides.openmp.num_threads` is read by the host renderer — so an aliased thread count silently degraded to 1 thread. Consumers of a knob cannot key off a name that changes every regeneration. This schema is a DECLARATIVE COPY: the validator holds the same names as constants and enforces them without file I/O, so an unreadable schema cannot fail-open a running gate. The alias -> canonical table is the load-bearing artifact and lives in the validator, because draft-07 cannot express `this misspelling means that key`. The knob layer stays OPEN (`additionalProperties: true`) — Tune's exploration space is the whole point of a knob, and only the parallelization family is pinned.

abstract.description: Language-independent knobs. Open by design; only the parallelization family below is pinned.

parallelization.description: The parallel execution model, as a FLAT string. The mapping form (`{method: openmp, apply_to: parallelizable_loops}`) is rejected by the canonical validator: decompose it into this key plus `parallel_scope` / `parallel_granularity`. Compared case-insensitively when target.backend=openmp, because a live certified IR carries `OpenMP`.

parallel_scope.description: Which loops the parallelization covers — prose naming them (e.g. `the ghost-fill loops of periodic_copy_x and periodic_copy_y`) or a symbolic value such as `parallelizable_loops`. This is the knob the Generate producer reads to decide where directives go.

parallel_granularity.description: Optional. The nesting level parallelism is applied at (e.g. `loop_level`, `interface_loop`).

backend_overrides.description: Per-backend override values, keyed by backend. Only the `openmp` key's members are pinned.

num_threads.description: Thread count. CANONICAL — `tools/runner_renderer.py` reads exactly this key, so `threads` / `threads_per_rank` are silently ignored and the run degrades to 1 thread.

chunk_size.description: Schedule chunk size; 0 means the implementation default.

collapse.description: Number of nested loops to collapse into one iteration space.

x-forbidden-examples-note: draft-07 rejects only the TYPE violations on the pinned keys (a string `num_threads`, a mapping `parallelization`). Every alias below is rejected by the canonical validator alone, since a rename remedy cannot be expressed as a schema constraint. Absent sections and novel (non-alias) knob names PASS both — the gate is a closed-table check, not a whitelist.
x-forbidden-examples: abstract.parallelization: {method: openmp, apply_to: parallelizable_loops}  -> flat string + abstract.parallel_scope
abstract.parallelization: {scheme: openmp, default_schedule: static}  -> flat string + abstract.parallel_scope + backend_overrides.openmp.schedule
backend_overrides.openmp.num_threads: "8"  -> an integer, not a string
